items.title: Ex-Madras HC Justice V Sivagnanam untraceable in Nepal after floods; bar body seeks CJI intervention
items.summary: Former Madras High Court Justice V Sivagnanam has been untraceable in Nepal since flash floods hit the country. The Delhi Tamil Advocates Association has implored Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to intervene and ask the government authorities to help trace the retired judge and facilitate his safe return to India. In a letter written to the CJI on August 30, the bar body said that while fellow pilgrims were rescued, Justice Sivagnanam could not be reached. He had last contacted his wife on August 26. As per the letter, "The persons travelling in another bus, who were rescued near the APF Nepal Border Outpost at Timure, have informed the family that Justice Sivagnanam’s bus was only about 100–200 metres away from theirs. The family and our Association are, therefore, gravely concerned about his safety and whereabouts." Justice Sivagnanam had a career spanning 34 years in the judiciary. After his retirement, he was designated Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court in July 2025.

items.title: Karnataka minister calls Islam superior to other religions, sparks BJP backlash
items.summary: Karnataka Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddy has triggered a political controversy after describing Islam as "superior to all other religions" while addressing a mass marriage ceremony in Kukanur, Koppal district, held to mark Prophet Muhammad's birth anniversary. Rayareddy said Islam was a "great religion" that promoted humanity and was "scientific in nature," teaching people how to live without becoming religious fanatics or casteists. It is unclear when the event was held. He said many misconceptions were being spread about Islam and that he was willing to study the Quran, adding that the text was meant for all of humanity and not just Muslims. The minister also said he wished to undertake the Hajj pilgrimage but had not had the opportunity to do so, noting that one had to convert to Islam. He said he rarely visits mutts or temples himself, though he tries to study the history of different religions, including Abrahamic faiths. Rayareddy clarified that good principles exist in all religions and that similar practices are followed in temples as well.
